doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Avoiding 52nd Street clubs because of smoke
summary: He never went to the 52nd Street clubs because he dislikes smoke, though he played Birdland and Bop City.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well New York was a pretty hot town, 52nd Street and all of that?

All those places. But oddly enough, and I almost hate to admit it, I never went there. I don’t drink and I don’t smoke, and I couldn’t stand the smoke in most of the clubs you know. And I played in Birdland with Count Basie and I played in another place called © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-

Bop City with Herbie Fields’ band. And I always had difficulty with the smoke in those places. So I tried to stay away as much as possible, and I never went into the clubs on 52nd Street. And it’s almost criminal that I was here when they were running, that I was there rather when they were functioning, but I just never went. I admired the guys who were working there, they were tremendous.
The jam session was a big part of learning music.
